title: Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund
summary: AIC scheme for eligible Singapore seniors needing mobility and assistive-device support, transport support, or home healthcare items.
claims: Use SMF as an official source to check mobility aid, assistive device, transport, and home healthcare item support.
Eligibility should be verified on AIC before presenting any final subsidy amount or application decision.

title: Home Caregiving Grant
summary: AIC monthly cash payout scheme for eligible families caring for persons with moderate to severe disabilities at home.
claims: HCG can be checked when a transcript indicates ongoing home caregiving expenses or disability-related care needs.
The user's eligibility and payout tier must be verified against AIC's current page.

title: Caregivers Training Grant
summary: AIC grant that subsidises approved caregiver training courses for eligible care recipients and caregivers.
claims: CTG is relevant when the transcript implies the caregiver needs training for mobility, daily living, dementia, or home-care tasks.
Only approved courses and current AIC rules should be treated as verified eligibility facts.

title: ElderFund
summary: AIC discretionary assistance scheme for lower-income Singapore Citizens with severe disability and long-term care needs.
claims: ElderFund should be considered only as an official lead when severe disability and long-term care cost concerns are present.
Means-test, disability assessment, and interaction with other long-term care schemes must be verified on AIC.

title: Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly
summary: AIC disability assistance scheme for older Singaporeans with severe disabilities who may need help with care costs.
claims: IDAPE can be surfaced as an official scheme lead for older care recipients with severe disability language in the transcript.
Eligibility and interaction with ElderFund, ElderShield, or CareShield Life must be checked on current AIC pages.

title: CareShield Life / ElderShield
summary: Long-term care insurance schemes that may provide payouts for eligible people with severe disability.
claims: CareShield Life and ElderShield are relevant when transcripts mention severe disability or inability to perform activities of daily living.
The agent must not claim eligibility without current scheme membership and disability assessment details.

title: Assistive Technology Fund
summary: SG Enable scheme for assistive technology support for eligible persons with disabilities.
claims: ATF is relevant for disability-related assistive technology or device needs.
Final eligibility and subsidy details must be verified with SG Enable.

title: 7 Fall Prevention Tips for Seniors and Caregivers
summary: HealthHub caregiver-facing fall prevention and home-safety information for seniors.
claims: Use this as a health-education source for fall prevention and home safety, not as a grant eligibility source.

title: MindSG: Managing Dementia As A Caregiver
summary: HealthHub MindSG caregiver information for supporting elderly parents with dementia.
claims: Use this as an official education source when dementia caregiving support is relevant.

title: Knowing Available Care Options
summary: AIC caregiver page covering available care options, care services, support groups, and financial grants.
claims: This is a useful official navigational source when the task is broad care planning rather than a single grant.

title: MediSave Care
summary: AIC long-term care scheme that allows eligible severely disabled Singapore Citizens or PRs to make monthly cash withdrawals from MediSave.
claims: MediSave Care is relevant when transcripts mention severe disability, long-term care costs, home care services, or nursing-home fees.
Eligibility depends on current AIC rules, MediSave balance, age, citizenship or PR status, and severe disability assessment.

title: MediFund
summary: MOH safety-net scheme for Singaporeans who face difficulty paying remaining healthcare bills after subsidies, insurance, and MediSave.
claims: MediFund should be surfaced when care notes mention inability to pay medical, hospital, community hospital, or approved long-term care bills.
Applications are assessed by the relevant MediFund-approved institution and should be discussed with medical social workers.

title: MediShield Life
summary: MOH basic national health insurance scheme for Singapore Citizens and PRs that helps with large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments.
claims: MediShield Life is useful context for hospitalisation or major-bill questions, but exact claim limits and payable amounts must be verified on MOH.
Do not present MediShield Life as a cash grant; it is insurance with claim limits, deductibles, and co-payment rules.

title: MediSave Outpatient Care and CDMP
summary: MOH page covering MediSave outpatient use, including MediSave500/700 support for CDMP chronic-condition treatment.
claims: Use this when transcripts mention outpatient chronic-condition bills, CDMP conditions, medication follow-up, or GP clinic costs.
Current annual withdrawal limits and eligible conditions should be verified on MOH before giving final guidance.

title: Community Health Assist Scheme
summary: MOH scheme that enables Singapore Citizens, including Pioneer and Merdeka Generation cardholders, to receive subsidies at participating GP and dental clinics.
claims: CHAS is relevant for outpatient GP, dental, preventive, and chronic-care affordability questions.
Card tier, enrolled clinic status, Healthier SG status, and current subsidy caps must be verified.

title: Enhanced Home Personal Care
summary: AIC home-care service that provides daily personal care, routine support, maintenance exercises, and respite options for seniors at home.
claims: Enhanced Home Personal Care is relevant when transcripts mention caregiver burnout, daily-living help, falls monitoring, medication reminders, or short breaks.
Government subsidies require Singapore Citizen or PR status and are means-tested; referral route should be checked on AIC.

title: Home Therapy
summary: AIC service for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy at home for frail or homebound seniors who need rehabilitation.
claims: Home Therapy is relevant for post-stroke, mobility, swallowing, speech, and daily-living rehabilitation needs when clinic travel is difficult.
Subsidy eligibility and referral requirements should be verified on AIC.

title: Day Care
summary: AIC centre-based day care and dementia day care service for seniors who need supervision, activities, basic care, and caregiver respite.
claims: Day Care is relevant when caregivers need daytime supervision, structured activities, dementia day care, or respite while working.
Subsidies are means-tested and eligibility should be verified with AIC or the care provider.

title: Home-based Respite Care
summary: AIC short-term respite service for caregivers managing loved ones receiving home palliative care or compassionate discharge support.
claims: HBRC is relevant only for palliative-care or compassionate-discharge contexts and should not be generalized to all respite needs.
AIC notes that from 1 April 2026, people needing home-based respite care can apply for Enhanced Home Personal Care services.

title: Disability Support
summary: SG Enable disability-support entry point for persons with disabilities, caregivers, and professionals to find schemes, services, and planning resources.
claims: Use SG Enable Disability Support as an official navigation source for disability schemes, caregiver planning, and service options.
Specific scheme eligibility still needs verification on the relevant SG Enable or Enabling Guide page.

title: Rehabilitation after Stroke: Physiotherapy
summary: HealthHub stroke physiotherapy education source for mobility, balance, walking aids, and rehabilitation after stroke.
claims: Use this as official education context when post-stroke mobility or rehabilitation needs appear in a transcript.
The agent should not prescribe exercises; it should route to clinician or therapist guidance.

title: Rehabilitation after Stroke: Swallowing Difficulties
summary: HealthHub education source on swallowing difficulties after stroke and the role of speech therapists, dietitians, and caregiver training.
claims: Use this as safety education when transcripts mention choking, coughing during meals, swallowing difficulty, or feeding-tube care after stroke.
Swallowing concerns should be escalated to qualified clinical review rather than handled as general advice.

title: Heart Failure - Monitoring Weight and Blood Pressure
summary: HealthHub heart-failure education source on daily weight monitoring, blood pressure tracking, and signs that may need clinical follow-up.
claims: Use this for official education context when transcripts mention heart failure, sudden weight gain, blood-pressure checks, or fluid retention.
Escalation thresholds and medication changes should be verified with the care team.
